passage:
Aditi walked into the Class 9 lab just as Ishita's table burst out laughing. Aditi's stomach dropped. Her hair? The stain on her sleeve? She slid onto the far stool and kept her eyes on the burner.
At lunch she had messaged Ishita, 'partners for the project?' The two ticks had turned blue at 1:10. It was now 2:40. No reply.
So that's it, Aditi thought. They've decided.
When Ishita leaned over and whispered, 'Did you see Harshit's goggles? They're on upside down,' Aditi only shrugged and said, 'I'm working with Neel.'
Ishita blinked. 'Oh. Okay.' She turned back to her table.
Aditi stared at the flame, hands cold, sure now that she had been right all along.

qa.q: At what time did the ticks on Aditi's message turn blue?
qa.a: The two ticks turned blue at 1:10.

qa.q: What was Aditi afraid the laughter meant?
qa.a: She feared the table was laughing at her hair or the stain on her sleeve, and took the missing reply to mean they had decided to drop her.

qa.q: What could Aditi try at this stage to test her fear?
qa.a: She could treat her first reading as a guess, laugh at the goggles with Ishita and simply ask about the project, since the joke showed the laughter wasn't about her.

qa.q: How might Ishita experience Aditi's shrug and 'I'm working with Neel'?
qa.a: Ishita reached out with a joke and got a cold reply, so she may feel brushed off and conclude Aditi doesn't want her as a partner 😔

grounding: It shows a lonely teenager reading a laugh and a slow reply as dislike, then acting guarded in a way that pushes her friend away.

passage:
Dear Bidisha Apu,
You said to write when things feel heavy, so here I am.
School has been strange since you left. On Monday I posted in the class group asking if anyone had the chemistry notes. Forty minutes, nothing. Then Rumana replied 'check the drive' with no emoji. Not even a smiley. I read that about ten times.
At lunch, Tasnim said something and everyone laughed just as I sat down. I'm almost sure it was about me. So now I eat quickly and go to the library, and when people talk to me I answer in one word, and they've mostly stopped talking to me. Which proves it, doesn't it?
Or does it? I can't tell anymore.
Write back soon 🥺
Nazia

qa.q: What did Rumana reply after forty minutes?
qa.a: Rumana replied 'check the drive' with no emoji.

qa.q: Why did Nazia read Rumana's reply about ten times?
qa.a: Nazia was searching it for signs of dislike, because a lonely, worried mind was treating a missing smiley as a threat.

qa.q: What could help Nazia step out of this loop?
qa.a: Nazia could list other reasons for the slow reply and the laugh, and try one warmer answer at lunch to see what actually happens 🙂

qa.q: How might the classmates see Nazia's one-word answers?
qa.a: They might think Nazia wants to be left alone, so they talk less, which then feels like proof of the rejection Nazia feared.

grounding: It shows a teenager reading a late reply and a laugh as dislike, becoming guarded and quiet in a way that seems to confirm the fear.
